label: UniFi Switch Enterprise 8 PoE
description: Ubiquiti USW-Enterprise-8-PoE - 8x 2.5GbE RJ45 all PoE+ (120W), 2x 10G SFP+; Layer 3 UniFi switch.
notes: Each figure is the vendor's. https://dl.ui.com/ds/usw-enterprise-8-poe_ds.pdf (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 526,714 B, 2 pp) prints "Networking interface (8) 1/2.5 GbE RJ45 / (2) 1/10 Gbps SFP+", "PoE interface (8) PoE/PoE+ (Pins 1, 2+; 3, 6-)", "Max. PoE+ wattage per port by PSE 32W" and "Max PoE power 120W"; https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/switching/usw-enterprise-8-poe (HTTP 200, 648,955 B, rendered spec table, read 2026-11-21) prints the same counts as rows ("2.5 GbE RJ45 = 8 (All PoE+) (2.5G/1G/100/10M)", "PoE+ = 8", "Total PoE Availability = 120W"). Before this correction no copper port on this row declared poeOut. The engine's isPoePse() heuristic still gave each one a PSE, but at the undeclared 802.3af default of 15.4 W (engine/media.js, `if (port.poeOut === null ...) port.poeOut = 15.4`), so the faceplate tooltip and the port detail panel reported "PoE out 15.4 W" on a port the datasheet rates 802.3at at 32 W by PSE - the one figure an operator reads when asking whether the socket can power a 25.5 W AP. All 8 copper ports now declare the vendor's per-port PSE ceiling (32 W) and the vendor's class word ("PoE/PoE+"), and the row declares poe-pse/802.3af/802.3at instead of leaving the per-port figure to the undeclared-port default. The SFP+ cages are not PSE ports and stay undeclared.
